subject: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask

Team —

We kicked off an ops review yesterday and a recurring theme is that we lack a single pane that shows where per-route SLA exposure correlates with missing instrumentation/ownership. Customers hit slow tails that look like infra problems, but tracing shows many are missing per-route sampling or have outdated owner metadata.

Ask: can the Console include a one-off "SLA gap heatmap" tile + a small exportable inventory of routes with empty owner metadata? Minimum acceptance criteria:
- Heatmap rows: routes (grouped by service), columns: SLA metric buckets (p99 latency, error rate, token cost spike) for the last 72h
- Highlight routes with no owner or owner tag == "unassigned"
- Export button that produces a CSV (route, owner, p50/p95/p99 latency, last-instrumented-at)
- Sample sketch attached (sample-heatmap-sketch.png) and a raw endpoint list (endpoint-list.csv) for the initial MVP

Why now: we have two enterprise customers in trial asking for per-route clarity before we enable chargeback. Ops wants this to triage allocation and ownership faster.

Constraints: keep the compute/timebox small — we should use sampled traces and existing telemetry aggregates rather than full trace replays for MVP.

Can you each weigh in on feasibility and rough sprint estimate? If feasible, I propose we target an internal canary by 2028-11-20.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Observability & Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Nov 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask

Jonas —

This is doable as an MVP but a few clarifying Qs:
1) Data sources: do you want the heatmap computed from the same aggregated time-series we already have in the console (metrics store), or are we pulling from sampling+trace aggregation (which will give better p99 accuracy but is heavier)?
2) Ownership tagging: we have three owner fields (route_owner, product_tier_owner, infra_owner). Which one should drive the "unassigned" highlight?

Proposal: use metrics store for p50/p95 and sampling/traces for p99. Mark route_owner as primary for now. That will let us build the heatmap fast and backfill p99 later.

I attached endpoint-list.csv with a suggested initial route filter (top 500 by 72h request volume). Also added a quick notes doc "sla-metrics-spec.md" to the attachments.

Estimate: engineering MVP ~ 6 dev-days (1 frontend, 1 backend, 1 infra spike to add export endpoint) + 2 QA days. Canary target: 2028-11-21 if we start next week.

—Ben

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Nov 2028 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask

On Fri, Nov 2, 2028 at 10:07 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Jonas —
>
> This is doable as an MVP but a few clarifying Qs: ...

Jonas/Ben —

Couple of operational notes from observability side:
- For p99, sampling bias matters (some customers enable aggressive sampling). For the MVP, we should expose a small confidence indicator per cell (low/medium/high) based on sample counts. That avoids false positives.
- Suggest a sliding 72h window with a 1h rollup resolution; it balances freshness and compute.
- Regarding owner fields: I support using route_owner as the primary gating property. We should also surface secondary owners in the export so CS knows who to loop in.
- Backfills: if route_owner is empty but product_tier_owner exists, mark route as "candidate owner" in the CSV and add a note in the UI.

I can scope the telemetry changes (sample-count exposure + owner crosswalk) in ~3 infra-days. Will need help from backend on an aggregator endpoint.

—Soojin

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Nov 2028 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask

Team —

Feasibility check: Ben's estimate looks reasonable. A couple of additions from Product/PM perspective:
- We should include a small "risk classification" column (Operational / Instrumentation / Capacity) derived from priorities: missing owner -> Operational, low-sample-count -> Instrumentation, cost spike -> Capacity. This will help CS prioritize fixes.
- Put a toggle in the canary to restrict to specific orgs (Gridlytics and Acme) so we can demo without exposing global data.
- I'll create a tracking ticket (JIRA-OPS-1427) and a short design doc (drive link below) that can be linked from the tile for context.

Timeline: if infra/engine starts this week, we can ship an internal canary on 2028-11-20 and a staged rollout to a small set of tenants by 2028-12-04.

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2bHeatmapDraft

—Marcus
Product Manager, Console

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@gridlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Nov 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA gap heatmap + route ownership inventory — quick ask

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick summary and immediate next steps:
- Scope: MVP = metrics-store p50/p95 + sampled p99 (confidence indicator) + route_owner primary + CSV export with candidate-owner fallback
- Owners: Ben/Infra will wire export and the heatmap endpoint (Ben: start Monday). Soojin: sample-count exposure + owner crosswalk (infra days listed)
- PM: Marcus will file JIRA-OPS-1427 and add the design stub (drive link)
- Canary: target internal canary 2028-11-20; tenant canary (Gridlytics + Acme) by 2028-12-04

Olivia — looping you in so Gridlytics can review scope (we'll only enable as canary if you opt-in). If you'd like, we'll schedule a 30m walkthrough after the internal canary.

I'll update the ticket with the attachments and the endpoint-list.csv we agreed on.

Jonas
